=== .github/workflows/web-e2e.yml ===
name: Web E2E Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: 'Git ref to checkout (tag, branch, or SHA)'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions: {}

jobs:
  web-e2e:
    name: Web E2E Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

      ipfs:
        image: ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0
        ports:
          - 5001:5001
          - 8080:8080
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "ipfs id"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
          --health-start-period 30s

      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7.0.0
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}

      - name: Setup pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@48b55a011bda9f5d6aeb4c2d9c7362e8dae4041e # v6.4.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Configure Kubo CORS for browser-based recovery test
        run: |
          # Allow browser cross-origin requests to Kubo gateway (needed by recovery.html)
          docker exec $(docker ps -q --filter ancestor=ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0) ipfs config --json API.HTTPHeaders.Access-Control-Allow-Origin '["*"]'
          docker exec $(docker ps -q --filter ancestor=ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0) ipfs config --json API.HTTPHeaders.Access-Control-Allow-Methods '["GET","POST","OPTIONS"]'
          docker exec $(docker ps -q --filter ancestor=ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0) ipfs config --json Gateway.HTTPHeaders.Access-Control-Allow-Origin '["*"]'
          docker exec $(docker ps -q --filter ancestor=ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0) ipfs config --json Gateway.HTTPHeaders.Access-Control-Allow-Methods '["GET","POST","OPTIONS"]'
          # Restart Kubo to apply config (kill + Docker auto-restarts)
          docker restart $(docker ps -q --filter ancestor=ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0)
          # Wait for Kubo to be healthy again
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if docker exec $(docker ps -q --filter ancestor=ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0) ipfs id > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Kubo ready with CORS configured"
              break
            fi
            sleep 2
          done

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e exec playwright install chromium --with-deps

      - name: Install mock-ipns-routing dependencies
        run: |
          cd tools/mock-ipns-routing
          npm install
          npm run build

      - name: Build packages (excluding desktop)
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api-client build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build
        env:
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000

      - name: Create .env files for Web E2E
        run: |
          # Web app .env (for Vite dev server)
          echo "VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID=${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}" > apps/web/.env
          echo "VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000" >> apps/web/.env
          # API .env (for NestJS)
          echo "NODE_ENV=test" > apps/api/.env
          echo "DB_HOST=localhost" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "DB_PORT=5432" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "DB_USERNAME=postgres" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "DB_PASSWORD=REDACTED >> apps/api/.env
          echo "DB_DATABASE=cipherbox_test" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "JWT_SECRET=e2e-test-jwt-secret-key-for-ci" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5173" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "IPFS_PROVIDER=local" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL=http://localhost:5001" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "IPFS_LOCAL_GATEWAY_URL=http://localhost:8080" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://localhost:3001" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "REDIS_HOST=localhost" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "REDIS_PORT=6379" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY=${{ secrets.IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY }}" >> apps/api/.env

      - name: Run Web E2E tests
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e test
        env:
          CI: true
          # Database configuration
          DB_HOST: localhost
          DB_PORT: 5432
          DB_USERNAME: postgres
          DB_PASSWORD: postgres
          DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_test
          NODE_ENV: test
          # IPFS configuration
          IPFS_PROVIDER: local
          IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL: http://localhost:5001
          IPFS_LOCAL_GATEWAY_URL: http://localhost:8080
          # API configuration
          JWT_SECRET: e2e-test-jwt-secret-key-for-ci
          CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: http://localhost:5173
          # IPNS delegated routing (mock service)
          DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL: http://localhost:3001
          # Redis for BullMQ job scheduling
          REDIS_HOST: localhost
          REDIS_PORT: 6379
          # Web app configuration (needed for Web3Auth initialization)
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          # Test-login endpoint (bypasses Core Kit, uses deterministic keypair)
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          SDK_E2E_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          # Web3Auth test credentials (fallback if TEST_LOGIN_SECRET not set)
          WEB3AUTH_TEST_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.WEB3AUTH_TEST_EMAIL }}
          WEB3AUTH_TEST_OTP: ${{ secrets.WEB3AUTH_TEST_OTP }}

      - name: Upload Playwright report on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: |
            tests/web-e2e/playwright-report/
            tests/web-e2e/test-results/
          retention-days: 7

=== web-e2e README ===
<!-- generated-by: gsd-doc-writer -->

# CipherBox E2E Tests

End-to-end tests for CipherBox using Playwright.

## Setup

1. Install dependencies:

   ```bash
   pnpm install
   ```

2. Install Playwright browsers:

   ```bash
   pnpm exec playwright install
   ```

3. Configure environment (optional):

   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env
   # Edit .env with your test configuration
   ```

## Running Tests

### All tests

```bash
pnpm test
```

### Specific test file

```bash
pnpm test tests/wallet-login.spec.ts
```

### Single browser

```bash
pnpm test --project=chromium
```

### Headed mode (visible browser)

```bash
pnpm test:headed
```

### Debug mode

```bash
pnpm test:debug
```

### View last report

```bash
pnpm test:report
```

## Test Structure

```text
tests/web-e2e/
├── fixtures/              # Static test assets
│   └── files/             # Sample files for upload tests (images, PDFs, video, audio)
├── page-objects/          # Page Object Model classes
│   ├── login.page.ts      # Login page interactions
│   ├── base.page.ts       # Base page helpers
│   ├── dialogs/           # Dialog page objects
│   ├── file-browser/      # File browser page objects
│   └── pages/             # Other page objects
├── tests/                 # Test specs (flat, no subdirectories)
│   ├── wallet-login.spec.ts
│   ├── full-workflow.spec.ts
│   ├── sharing-workflow.spec.ts
│   ├── mfa-flows.spec.ts
│   ├── recovery.spec.ts
│   ├── search-workflow.spec.ts
│   ├── recycle-bin.spec.ts
│   ├── conflict-detection.spec.ts
│   ├── batch-download.spec.ts
│   ├── writable-shares.spec.ts
│   ├── invite-link-workflow.spec.ts
│   ├── media-preview.spec.ts
│   ├── streaming-playback.spec.ts
│   └── journey-timing.spec.ts
├── utils/                 # Test utilities
│   ├── wallet-login-helpers.ts  # Mock wallet setup and login helpers
│   ├── api-helpers.ts           # API-level helpers
│   ├── cleanup-helpers.ts       # Account/data cleanup helpers
│   ├── conflict-helpers.ts      # Conflict scenario helpers
│   ├── mfa-helpers.ts           # MFA flow helpers
│   ├── multi-account-wallet.ts  # Multi-account wallet setup
│   └── test-files.ts            # Test file references
└── playwright.config.ts   # Playwright configuration
```

## Authentication in Tests

### Mock Wallet Pattern

Tests authenticate using `@johanneskares/wallet-mock`, which installs an EIP-6963 mock
provider in the browser. This avoids any real Web3Auth modal interaction and works fully
headless in CI.

Each test suite that requires authentication calls `setupMockWallet()` before navigating:

```typescript
import { setupMockWallet, createTestAccount } from '../utils/wallet-login-helpers';

const account = createTestAccount(); // generates a random private key

test.beforeAll(async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext();
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await setupMockWallet(page, account); // must be called before navigation
  await page.goto('/');
});
```

For deterministic tests (e.g., wallet login flow), a well-known Hardhat account key is
used instead of a random key.

### No Storage State

There is no global setup or stored `.auth/user.json` state. Each test suite sets up its
own wallet-authenticated session from scratch using the mock wallet.

## CI Integration

E2E tests run automatically on GitHub Actions for every push and pull request to `main`.

### CI Workflow

The E2E workflow (`.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml`):

1. Starts PostgreSQL and IPFS services
2. Installs dependencies and Playwright browsers
3. Builds all packages
4. Runs E2E tests in headless Chromium
5. Uploads test artifacts (reports, videos, screenshots) on failure

### CI Environment

- **Authentication**: All tests use the mock wallet — no manual Web3Auth interaction required
- **Services**: PostgreSQL and IPFS run as Docker containers
- **Parallelism**: Tests run sequentially (`workers: 1`) to share a single browser session

### Running Tests Locally Like CI

```bash
# Set CI environment variable
CI=true pnpm test
```

This will:

- Use HTML reporter (instead of interactive list)
- Fail if any tests are marked `.only`
- Always start a fresh dev server (never reuses an existing one)

## Notes

- **Chromium only**: Tests target Desktop Chrome; other browsers are not configured
- **Sequential execution**: `fullyParallel: false`, `workers: 1` — tests run one at a time
- **No retries**: Flakiness is fixed at the source, not masked with retries
- **External target**: Set `BASE_URL` to a staging/production URL to skip local server startup
- **Protected Routes**: Dashboard and file browser routes require wallet authentication

## Troubleshooting

### Mock Wallet Not Detected

# CipherBox E2E Tests

End-to-end tests for CipherBox using Playwright.

## Setup

1. Install dependencies:


## Authentication in Tests

### Mock Wallet Pattern

Tests authenticate using `@johanneskares/wallet-mock`, which installs an EIP-6963 mock
provider in the browser. This avoids any real Web3Auth modal interaction and works fully
headless in CI.

Each test suite that requires authentication calls `setupMockWallet()` before navigating:

```typescript
import { setupMockWallet, createTestAccount } from '../utils/wallet-login-helpers';

const account = createTestAccount(); // generates a random private key

test.beforeAll(async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext();
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await setupMockWallet(page, account); // must be called before navigation
  await page.goto('/');
});
```

For deterministic tests (e.g., wallet login flow), a well-known Hardhat account key is
used instead of a random key.

### No Storage State

There is no global setup or stored `.auth/user.json` state. Each test suite sets up its
own wallet-authenticated session from scratch using the mock wallet.

## CI Integration

E2E tests run automatically on GitHub Actions for every push and pull request to `main`.

### CI Workflow

The E2E workflow (`.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml`):

1. Starts PostgreSQL and IPFS services
2. Installs dependencies and Playwright browsers
3. Builds all packages
4. Runs E2E tests in headless Chromium
5. Uploads test artifacts (reports, videos, screenshots) on failure

### CI Environment

- **Authentication**: All tests use the mock wallet — no manual Web3Auth interaction required
- **Services**: PostgreSQL and IPFS run as Docker containers
- **Parallelism**: Tests run sequentially (`workers: 1`) to share a single browser session

### Running Tests Locally Like CI

```bash
# Set CI environment variable
CI=true pnpm test
```

This will:

- Use HTML reporter (instead of interactive list)
- Fail if any tests are marked `.only`
- Always start a fresh dev server (never reuses an existing one)

## Notes

- **Chromium only**: Tests target Desktop Chrome; other browsers are not configured
- **Sequential execution**: `fullyParallel: false`, `workers: 1` — tests run one at a time
- **No retries**: Flakiness is fixed at the source, not masked with retries
- **External target**: Set `BASE_URL` to a staging/production URL to skip local server startup
- **Protected Routes**: Dashboard and file browser routes require wallet authentication

## Troubleshooting

### Mock Wallet Not Detected

`setupMockWallet()` must be called before any `page.goto()`. If the wallet is not detected,
ensure the call order in `beforeAll`/`beforeEach` is correct.

### Web App Not Starting

- Verify `pnpm install` has been run at the monorepo root
- Check that ports 3000 (API), 3001 (mock IPNS routing), and 5173 (web) are free
- The mock IPNS routing service must be built first: `pnpm build` from the workspace root

### Tests Timing Out

- Check that the backend API is running and accessible at `http://localhost:3000`
- For CI, verify the `web-e2e.yml` workflow services started successfully

content.text:
I have the full, honest picture. Here it is.

## The full web-e2e suite is running locally, but it does not pass — and cannot, on this branch

**Result:** 6 passed / 19 failed / 183 did not run (208 total, 22.7 min).

This is **not an infra problem and not a Phase 68 regression.** The stack came up correctly (Postgres, Kubo, redis:6380, mock-ipns all healthy; SIWE + test-login both work — I verified test-login returns a JWT). The app itself throws.

### Root cause (evidence-backed)
The page snapshot at the moment of failure shows the login screen with this alert:
```
alert: not implemented — phase 63 (root Node initialization via Node codec)
```
- Source: `apps/web/src/hooks/useAuth.ts:210` — new-user login can't initialize the root vault Node, so the app never reaches `/files`. Every login-dependent test then times out on `page.waitForURL('**/files')`.
- `git blame` → introduced by **commit `b2dba554a` "unified Node codec … (#578)" — Phase 62** (2026-06-29), days before Phase 68. 68-11 only added the `rotationHighWater` injection nearby; it did not create this.
- It's not one stub — there are **17 `not implemented — phase 63` throws** across `packages/sdk/src/client.ts` + `apps/web/src` covering the whole read-chain runtime: root Node init, navigation, file preview, download, streaming, shared-folder nav, metadata resolution.

The 6 that pass are all `wallet-login.spec.ts` UI-state checks (button visible, connector list, SIWE initiates) — none complete a login.

### What this means
The v2.0 milestone was built plumbing-first with the web runtime deliberately stubbed (PROJECT.md: "behavioral paths stubbed to their owning phases per D-01"). The web app's actual login→vault→browse→download flow is not wired up yet, so the full web-e2e suite — which exercises exactly those flows — structurally can't go green until a read-chain web-integration phase lands. This is why Phase 68's own rotation specs were only ever authored + registered, never executed, and why the verifier marked the phase passed on the SDK-unit tier. web-e2e still passes on `main` (v1.1, functional) — the gap is specific to the in-progress v2.0 branch. I've saved this to memory so it isn't re-discovered the hard way.

Phase 68's rotation work itself remains correct and unit-verified (sdk-core 38/38, sdk 48/48); it just can't be exercised end-to-end through a UI that isn't wired yet.

### The honest bottom line
I can't hand you a green full web-e2e run on this branch without implementing that deferred read-chain layer (the 17 stubs) — which is effectively its own phase of work, not a Phase 68 gap. I'm not going to silently take that on.

208:**Goal**: Rotation correctly closes all three cryptographic revocation gaps — content-key rotation (CRIT-1), inner-grant re-mint (HIGH-3), concurrent-add merge (HIGH-4) — and survives a crash mid-walk; the `tests/sdk-e2e` crash-safety suite gates the phase.
212:**Requirements**: ROT-03, ROT-04, ROT-05, ROT-06, TEST-01

382:**Goal**: The web app uses `rotateReadFromNode` for all revocation-triggering mutations, persists a durable IndexedDB generation + seq high-water that survives page reload, and reconciles `folderTree` before any rotation publish.

436:**Goal**: The FUSE and WinFsp clients use symmetric key unwrap throughout, grant-root awareness gates scope-exit mutations, `Node` is a real Rust enum, and the Windows CI gate passes.
440:**Requirements**: TEST-03

The inventory came back decisive, and it's good news for tractability:

## Scope verdict: this is wiring, not building

The read-chain **runtime already exists** — `packages/core` (Node codec: `sealNode`/`unsealChildReadKey`/`unsealContent`), `sdk-core` (`navigateReadChain`, `loadFolderMetadata`, the rotation BFS walk), and `packages/sdk/share/shared-write.ts` (full read+write chain ops). The 18 `not implemented — phase 63` stubs are overwhelmingly **"call the existing primitives from `client.ts` + the web hooks."** Only two small new sdk-core primitives are genuinely missing (publish an empty **root** Node; a raw-`fileKey` download variant), plus **one real architecture decision**.

| Group | Verdict | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| (a) auth / root-Node-init (`useAuth.ts:210`) | PARTIAL — need a ~40-line "publish empty root Node" helper | ~0.5–1d |

| (c) file read: metadata / download / preview / streaming | Thin composition + one raw-key download adapter | ~1–2d |
| (d) shared-folder nav / download | Pure wiring to existing `navigateReadChain` / `moveInSharedFolder` (already implemented in sdk-core; the client stub's "also stubbed" comment is stale) | ~1–2d |

**Rough total: ~1 week.** Scope fence: the `addFile`/`replaceFile`/version stubs are **Phase 65 write-chain — out of scope**; this is read-path only.

**The one design decision:** `SealedChildRef` is a frozen schema with **no `kind` field**, so the file browser can't tell file-from-folder without a network hop per child. That needs an architecture call (carry kind in write-body at create time / lazy-resolve+cache / fetch-all-at-load) — I'll have the planner resolve it with a recommendation you review, unless you want to decide it upfront.

**Framing:** a new phase — goal "the v2.0 web app runs end-to-end (login→browse→download→share), with the **full web-e2e suite green** as the gate." That gate finally validates Phases 62–68 at runtime, which is your actual objective. I already have the research (the inventory above), so I can skip the research spawn.

30:- [x] **READ-02**: A grantee can navigate to a depth-`d` child via one ECIES unwrap then `O(depth)` symmetric AES, recovering content key/CID/mode at a file node; the read path distinguishes "soft behind, retry" from "hard revoked"
31:- [x] **READ-03**: Adding an item seals the child `readKey` under the parent `readKey` with no per-recipient fan-out; `reWrapForRecipients`/`addShareKeys` are deleted

content.text:
Important scope discovery — this changes the plan, so I'm surfacing it before proceeding.

## The runtime gap is bigger than read-chain: it's read **+** write

There are **two** stub families in the web/client runtime, not one:
- **17 `phase 63` (read-chain) stubs** — login/root-init, navigation, file download/preview/streaming, shared-folder read.
- **29 `phase 65` (write-chain) stubs** — file upload/create, replace, versions (restore/delete/download), bin re-link, share creation, permission upgrade, shared-folder write ops (rename/delete/move), owner file save, invite creation.

**46 runtime stubs total.** Same pattern as read: Phase 65 built the sdk-core write-chain, but the web+client *wiring* was deferred.

Why this matters for your goal: the web-e2e suite **creates its own content first** — nearly every spec uploads/creates/shares/deletes before it reads. So **read-chain wiring alone will not make the full suite green** — it gets login→browse→download→shared-read working, but upload/create/share/delete/versions still throw. To actually validate Phases 62–68 with a green web-e2e suite, both read *and* write integration are required.

Good news: like read, the write path is **wire-to-existing-sdk-core** (Phase 65 shipped the primitives; `shared-write.ts` already has `createSharedSubfolder`/`moveInSharedFolder` implemented), so it's tractable wiring — but it roughly doubles the effort (~2–3 weeks total across both).

I've already created **Phase 68.1** (read-chain). The write work is a natural **Phase 68.2**. Write depends on read being wired first (writes resolve parents via the read-chain), so the order is forced: read → write, and full web-e2e green is the exit gate on the *write* phase.

## 3. Reference implementations to copy

All in `packages/sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts` (the canonical write-chain, uses codec + injected `publishNodeFn`/`addToIpfsFn` seams):

- **`uploadToSharedFolder`** (:409) — mint fileKey/fileReadKey/fileWriteKey/Ed25519 keypair → `encryptAesGcm` content → `addToIpfsFn` → build `NodeContent` (raw fileKey inside sealed body) + file `Node` with `writeBody` → `sealNode` → publish seq `1n` → `sealChildReadKey` + `buildChildWriteLink` → `resealAndPublishParent`. **Copy for (a).**
- **`createSharedSubfolder`** (:298) — same pattern for folders. **Reference for owned createFolder.**
- **`updateSharedFile`** (:640) — mint new fileKey, re-encrypt, rebuild file Node preserving `id`/`generation`/`createdAt`/`originalVersions`, `sealNode`, `publishOrThrow` at `seq+1`. **Copy for (b) and (c).**
- **`moveInSharedFolder`** (:772) — `unsealParentWriteBody` both sides, `sealChildReadKey` under dest, `walkChildWriteKey`→`buildChildWriteLink` under dest, **publish dest before src** (dup-not-orphan). **Reference for (d) move + (f) move.**
- **`deleteFromSharedFolder`** (:600) — remove read-body by ipnsName, write-body by UUID `childId`.
- Helpers: `buildChildWriteLink` (:155), `walkChildWriteKey` (:183), `unsealParentWriteBody` (:202), `publishOrThrow` (:224), `resealAndPublishParent` (:247).

Seal/publish/CAS patterns:
- Owned read-chain re-seal on move already done: `client.ts moveItem` (:851) via `unsealChildReadKey`→`sealChildReadKey` — the read-chain analog to copy.
- CAS retry engine: `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` (`sdk-core/folder/registration.ts:159`) + `publishWithCas` (`sdk-core/cas.ts`). First-publish must embed `sequenceNumber: 1n` (strict gate; `createSubfolder`:119).
- Client seam wiring for shared ops: `buildSharedWriteContextFromState` (`client.ts:2095`) — honors BYO/external pinning via `pinWithMode` for content, routes node metadata through CipherBox.

Zeroization discipline (consistent D-09): mint keys as `let x: Uint8Array | null`; `.fill(0)` + null on success AND in `catch`/`finally`; **never zero caller-supplied buffers**; a derived key (e.g. `walkChildWriteKey` output) is zeroed by the deriver, a caller-supplied one is not (see `moveInSharedFolder` `didDeriveWriteKey`, :843-864).

# Phase 68.1 Research: Web Client Runtime Integration

## Summary — what this phase is

The v2.0 refactor shipped the read-chain (Phase 63) and write-chain (Phase 65) **in `packages/sdk-core` / `packages/sdk/share/shared-write.ts`**, but deferred the **web app + `CipherBoxClient` runtime wiring** as `throw new Error('not implemented — phase 63/65 (...)')` stubs. The full `tests/web-e2e` suite has therefore never run green since Milestone 4 started — a new-user login throws at `apps/web/src/hooks/useAuth.ts:210` (root Node init), so no login-dependent spec can pass. Measured baseline on this branch: **6/208 passed, 19 failed, 183 did-not-run** (only `wallet-login.spec.ts` UI-state tests pass).

**46 runtime stubs total: 17 `phase 63` (read) + 29 `phase 65` (write).**

### Three load-bearing findings

1. **Mostly wiring, with one genuine build.** The codec (`@cipherbox/core/node`) and read/write chains exist. Owned folder read/nav, shared read nav, and all 7 shared write ops (`shared-write.ts`) are implemented — the stubs are client/web wrappers. **EXCEPTION:** owned **file** create/update (`packages/sdk-core/src/file/index.ts` `createFileMetadata:119`, `updateFileMetadata:163`) are genuinely stubbed and must be **built in sdk-core** (heavily copyable from `uploadToSharedFolder`/`updateSharedFile`). This is the largest single work item.

2. **Two open architecture decisions** (see below) — must be resolved in the plan.

3. **Internal sequencing is forced: read-chain first.** Many `phase 65`-labelled stubs actually depend on the read-chain (subtree walks, key resolution): `downloadFromIpns`, version download, `collectChildKeys`, bin subtree collect, shared move/delete childId + dest-key resolution, and owned `createFolder` (`client.ts:760`, tagged phase 63). Plan waves: read foundation → owned file write-chain → owned/shared write wiring → web-e2e enablement.

### Stale comments to ignore
Several `client.ts` comments claim `updateSharedFile`/`moveInSharedFolder` are "stubbed in shared-write.ts" — they are **fully implemented**. The stubs are the client wrappers/web handlers, not the sdk-core primitives.

### Obsolete — delete, do not implement
`packages/sdk/src/reencrypt.ts` (`reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange`) — no callers; content self-seal removes re-encrypt-on-move.

---

## Open design decisions (resolve in the plan with a recommendation)

**D-1 (read): file-vs-folder kind discrimination.** `SealedChildRef` is a frozen schema with **no `kind` field** (`packages/core/src/node/types.ts`), so the file browser can't tell file from folder without a network hop per child. `isFileRef`/`isFilePointer` (`apps/web/src/utils/fileTypes.ts:137,145`) throw. Options: (a) resolve+cache kind at folder-load (only cheap if children are fetched anyway — they are on the read-chain path to a target, but a plain sibling listing does not fetch every child), (b) lazy-resolve+cache kind on demand (async icons), (c) carry kind in the in-memory `FolderState` populated at create time. Frozen read schema must not change.

**D-2 (write): owned `FolderState` model.** Owned `FolderState` (`packages/sdk/src/types.ts:164`) is **read-chain-only** — no `writeKey`, no `publishedNode`, uses `ipnsKeypair` directly. Shared `SharedFolderState` (`types.ts:205`) carries the full write-body model. Owned file write (a/b) needs either (i) extend the owned model to the write-body model like shared (clean copy of `shared-write.ts`, larger blast radius), or (ii) keep read-chain-only and thread the file `ipnsPrivateKey`/writeKey another way. This is the biggest open question and gates the owned-file-write plans.

---

## Read-chain inventory (phase 63 — 17 stubs)

### (a) auth / root-Node-init
- `apps/web/src/hooks/useAuth.ts:210` — new-user branch: publish an empty `kind:'root'` Node to the derived `rootIpnsName` via the codec, then register vault + set keys. **PARTIAL** in sdk-core: `initializeVault` (`core/vault/init.ts:43`), `publishVaultKeyBlob`/`loadVaultKeyBlob` (`sdk-core/vault/index.ts:30,74`) exist; MISSING a ~40-line "publish empty root Node" helper (template: `createSubfolder` in `sdk-core/folder/registration.ts:49`, but root variant: vault root keypair + `kind:'root'` + `writeBody{ipnsPrivateKey, writeChildren:[]}`).

### (b) navigation / read fan-out
- `packages/sdk/src/client.ts:478` — `ensureFolderLoaded(targetIpnsName)`: DFS from root through `folderTree`, unsealing each child readKey (and write-body for `ipnsPrivateKey`/writeKey). The self-heal chokepoint `requireFolder`(:492) depends on it. **Critical path.** Primitives EXIST: pattern in `rotateReadFromNode` (`sdk-core/rotation/engine.ts:990-1014`) + `navigateReadChain`; write-key recovery via `shared-write.ts` `walkChildWriteKey`/`unsealParentWriteBody`.
- `packages/sdk/src/client.ts:766` — `createFolder`: adapt `createSharedSubfolder` (`shared-write.ts:298`). (Tagged phase 63 though it needs write-body — entangled.)
- `apps/web/src/utils/fileTypes.ts:137,145` — `isFileRef`/`isFilePointer` → D-1.

### (c) owned file read
- `apps/web/src/services/file-metadata.service.ts:71` — `resolveFileMetadata`: single read-chain hop (unseal child readKey → fetch file Node → `unsealContent`). Pattern: `navigate.ts:145-171`, `client.ts:892-912`.
- `apps/web/src/services/download.service.ts:110` — `downloadFileFromIpns`: resolve `NodeContent`, fetch CID, decrypt with the **raw** `fileKey` (NOT legacy ECIES `downloadAndDecrypt`); `NodeContent.fileIv` is **base64** (`shared-write.ts:448,703`).
- `apps/web/src/hooks/useFilePreview.ts:53`, `useStreamingPreview.ts:46,50`, `DetailsDialog.tsx:104` — wiring on top of the resolver.

### (d) shared-folder read nav / download
- `packages/sdk/src/client.ts:2374` — `moveInSharedFolder` wrapper → wire to implemented `shared-write.ts:772` (comment is stale).
- `apps/web/src/hooks/useSharedNavigationActions.ts:78,88,126,136,145` — `navigateToShare`/`navigateToSubfolder`/`navigateUp`/`navigateToBreadcrumb`/`downloadSharedFile` → wire to `navigateReadChain` (`sdk-core/share/navigate.ts:106`) + `enumerateSharedSubtree` (`client.ts:2394`, implemented). `navigateToRoot`/`hideSharedItem` already work.

---

## Write-chain inventory (phase 65 — 29 stubs)

### (a) owned file create/upload — MISSING in sdk-core (build)
- `packages/sdk-core/src/file/index.ts:119` — `createFileMetadata` (**root blocker**). Copy `uploadToSharedFolder` (`shared-write.ts:409`).
- `packages/sdk-core/src/folder/registration.ts:278,303` — `addFileToFolder`/`addFilesToFolder`.
- `packages/sdk-core/src/upload/index.ts:168` — `uploadFile` implemented but throws via stubbed `createFileMetadata`.
- `apps/web/src/services/file-metadata.service.ts:35` — web mirror. `client.ts:1101/1276` `uploadFile`/`uploadFiles` already wired.

### (b) owned replace / update / owner save — MISSING in sdk-core (build)
- `packages/sdk-core/src/file/index.ts:163` — `updateFileMetadata` (**root blocker for b+c**). Copy `updateSharedFile` (`shared-write.ts:640`).
- `client.ts:1549` `replaceFile`; `apps/web/src/hooks/useFileOperations.ts:27`; `TextEditorDialog.tsx:166` (owner save; shared branch works).

### (c) file versions — mostly wiring (after b)
- `client.ts:1599/1645` `restoreFileVersion`/`deleteFileVersion`; `useFileVersions.ts:24,37`; `file-metadata.service.ts:78,107,118` pure transforms; reuse `mergeVersions` (`file/index.ts:88`, working). `downloadFromIpns` (`client.ts:1694`) + `VersionHistory.tsx:32` are read-chain (phase 63).

### (d) delete→bin re-link + move — small new logic, read-chain-gated
- `client.ts:241/252` `collectRemovedItemIpnsNames`/`collectBinEntryIpnsNames` (subtree walk). Bin core lifecycle (`deleteToBin:1795`, `restoreFromBin:1864`, `permanentDelete:1902`, `emptyBin:1928`) already implemented. `reencrypt.ts` obsolete → delete.

### (e) share / invite create — PARTIAL, read-chain-gated
- Grant primitives EXIST: `issueReadGrant`, `claimInvite` (`sdk-core/share/grant.ts`), `updateSharePermission` (`shared-write.ts:900`).
- MISSING: `apps/web/src/lib/crypto/key-wrapping.ts:21` `collectChildKeys` (subtree re-wrap — needs read-chain). `ShareDialog.tsx:128,152` share/upgrade; `invite.service.ts:84` `createInviteLink`.

### (f) shared-folder write ops — EXISTS in sdk-core → wiring
- All 7 ops implemented in `shared-write.ts`: `createSharedSubfolder:298`, `uploadToSharedFolder:409`, `renameInSharedFolder:555`, `deleteFromSharedFolder:600`, `updateSharedFile:640`, `moveInSharedFolder:772`, `updateSharePermission:900`.
- Client wrappers/web handlers stubbed: `client.ts:2268` `updateSharedFile`, `client.ts:2360` `moveInSharedFolder`; `useSharedWriteOps.ts:106/117/127/138/152` (rename/update/delete/move/batch). `renameItemHandler` = trivial (client method `renameInSharedFolder:2209` exists). delete/move/update need read-chain to resolve `childNodeId` (UUID) / dest-keys. Already wired: `useSharedWriteOps` upload/createFolder.

---

## Reference implementations (copy these)

Canonical write-chain — `packages/sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts` (uses codec + injected `publishNodeFn`/`addToIpfsFn` seams):
- `uploadToSharedFolder:409` → template for owned file create (a).
- `createSharedSubfolder:298` → owned createFolder.
- `updateSharedFile:640` → owned update + versions (b/c); preserves `id`/`generation`/`createdAt`/`originalVersions`, publishes `seq+1`.
- `moveInSharedFolder:772` → move (publish dest before src = dup-not-orphan).
- `deleteFromSharedFolder:600` → remove read-body by ipnsName, write-body by UUID `childId`.
- Helpers: `buildChildWriteLink:155`, `walkChildWriteKey:183`, `unsealParentWriteBody:202`, `publishOrThrow:224`, `resealAndPublishParent:247`.

Read-chain — `navigateReadChain` (`sdk-core/share/navigate.ts:106`); `loadFolderMetadata` (`sdk-core/folder/load.ts:54`); child-key re-seal in `client.ts moveItem:851-923` (`unsealChildReadKey`→`sealChildReadKey`).

CAS/publish — `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` (`sdk-core/folder/registration.ts:159`) + `publishWithCas` (`sdk-core/cas.ts`); **first publish must embed `sequenceNumber: 1n`** (strict gate). Client seam: `buildSharedWriteContextFromState` (`client.ts:2095`) routes content pins via `pinWithMode` (BYO/external) but node metadata through CipherBox.

Zeroization (D-09): mint keys as `let x: Uint8Array | null`; `.fill(0)`+null on success AND in `catch`/`finally`; **never zero caller-supplied buffers** (a derived key is zeroed by the deriver, a caller-supplied one is not — see `moveInSharedFolder` `didDeriveWriteKey:843-864`).

---

## Validation Architecture

The phase's exit gate is the **full `tests/web-e2e` Playwright suite** (login→browse→upload→download→share→delete→versions→rotation UX) — this is the primary, integration-tier validation and is what the user requires to prove Phases 62–68 at runtime.

- **Local/CI stack:** Postgres + Kubo (v0.42, CORS) + redis + mock-ipns-routing (`tools/mock-ipns-routing`); Playwright `webServer` auto-starts mock-ipns (:3001), API dev (:3000), web dev (:5173). Run: `pnpm test:web-e2e`. See `.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml` for the canonical recipe.
- **New sdk-core owned-file write-chain (`createFileMetadata`/`updateFileMetadata`)** is genuine new logic → cover with **Vitest** in `packages/sdk-core` (analog: existing `shared-write`/rotation suites), TDD-eligible.
- **SDK-tier round-trip:** the `tests/sdk-e2e` suite (real client→API IPNS) should stay green for any sdk-core write-chain change.
- **SC#5 doctrine:** ZERO `apps/web/src/*.spec.ts` — web behavior proven only by web-e2e; testable logic hoisted to SDK.
- **Backstop / non-inferable checks:** the `grep -rn "not implemented — phase 6"` emptiness assertion (SC#1); per-capability web-e2e specs already exist for most flows (upload, sharing, versions, recycle-bin, media, streaming, invite) — enable them by making the runtime real.

# Phase 68.1 — Validation Strategy

> Per-phase validation contract for feedback sampling during execution.

---

## Test Infrastructure

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Framework** | Vitest (`packages/sdk-core`, `packages/sdk`) for hoisted logic; Playwright (`tests/web-e2e`) for the integration/UI gate |
| **Config file** | existing (`packages/*/vitest.config.ts`, `tests/web-e2e/playwright.config.ts`) — no Wave 0 install |
| **Quick run command** | `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core exec vitest run <touched-file>` (targeted; seconds) |
| **Full suite command** | `pnpm test:web-e2e` (full Playwright suite — the phase exit gate) |
| **Estimated runtime** | targeted vitest ~seconds; full web-e2e ~20–25 min |

---

## Sampling Rate

- **After every task commit:** run the targeted Vitest file for sdk-core/sdk changes; `tsc -b` for web-only wiring (rebuild sdk-core/sdk dist first).
- **After every plan wave:** run the web-e2e spec(s) that the wave unblocks (e.g. read wave → `full-workflow` login/browse; write wave → upload/versions/sharing specs).
- **Before phase verification:** the FULL `pnpm test:web-e2e` suite must be green (all specs).
- **Max feedback latency:** targeted vitest < 30s; full web-e2e is the slow gate (run per wave + at phase end).

---

## Per-Task Verification Map

The planner assigns each task an `<automated>` verify command. Read-tier and web-wiring tasks verify via `tsc -b` + the unblocked web-e2e spec; the new sdk-core owned file write-chain (`createFileMetadata`/`updateFileMetadata`) verifies via new Vitest (TDD). The whole-phase gate is the full web-e2e suite (WEB-04 / SC#5).

| Task ID | Plan | Wave | Requirement | Test Type | Automated Command | Status |
|---------|------|------|-------------|-----------|-------------------|--------|
| (planner-assigned) | — | — | WEB-01..04 | vitest / tsc / playwright | per task `<automated>` | ⬜ pending |

*Status: ⬜ pending · ✅ green · ❌ red · ⚠️ flaky*

---

## Wave 0 Requirements

- Existing infrastructure covers all phase requirements (Vitest + Playwright already configured).
- New: a Vitest file for the built sdk-core owned file write-chain (`packages/sdk-core/src/__tests__/file/*.test.ts`) — created within the owned-file-write plan (TDD), not a separate Wave 0.

---

## Manual-Only Verifications

| Behavior | Requirement | Why Manual | Test Instructions |
|----------|-------------|------------|-------------------|
| Full web-e2e execution needs the local stack (Postgres + Kubo + redis + mock-ipns) | WEB-04 | Requires running services; not a pure unit gate | Bring up the stack per `.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml`, then `pnpm test:web-e2e` |

*All other phase behaviors have automated verification (Vitest units + Playwright specs).*

---

## Validation Sign-Off

- [ ] All tasks have `<automated>` verify or a Wave 0 dependency
- [ ] Sampling continuity: no 3 consecutive tasks without automated verify
- [ ] Wave 0 covers all MISSING references
- [ ] No watch-mode flags
- [ ] Feedback latency acceptable (targeted vitest fast; full web-e2e per wave + phase end)
- [ ] `nyquist_compliant: true` set once the plan's per-task map is filled

**Approval:** pending

</tdd_mode_active>

**Project instructions:** Read ./CLAUDE.md — string literals over TS enums, camelCase API, `Uint8Array` binary, canonical terminology, Web Crypto, never log/persist private keys.
</planning_context>

<what_this_phase_is>
This is the deferred **web + `CipherBoxClient` runtime wiring** to the already-shipped read-chain (Phase 63) and write-chain (Phase 65) sdk-core primitives. web-e2e has never run green since Milestone 4 started because these 46 stubs throw. RESEARCH.md has the complete inventory; trust it over stale in-code comments (several `client.ts` comments falsely claim `shared-write.ts` ops are stubbed — they are implemented).

**Two things you MUST resolve in the plan, each with a stated recommendation + rationale (the user reviews these):**
- **D-02 (kind discrimination):** `SealedChildRef` has no `kind` field (frozen schema — DO NOT change it). Decide how the file browser distinguishes file vs folder (lazy-resolve+cache / resolve-at-load / carry in in-memory FolderState). Put the chosen approach + why in the relevant plan.
- **D-03 (owned FolderState write model):** owned `FolderState` (types.ts:164) is read-chain-only (no writeKey/publishedNode); shared `SharedFolderState` (types.ts:205) carries the write-body model. Owned file write needs one resolved (extend owned model vs thread ipnsPrivateKey/writeKey read-chain-only). State the choice, rationale, and blast radius in the owned-file-write plan.

**The ONE genuine build** (everything else is wiring): the owned file write-chain in `packages/sdk-core/src/file/index.ts` (`createFileMetadata:119`, `updateFileMetadata:163`) — copy `shared-write.ts` `uploadToSharedFolder:409` / `updateSharedFile:640`. Make this a TDD plan with Vitest.
</what_this_phase_is>

<sequencing_and_waves>
Forced internal ordering (from RESEARCH): **read foundation → owned file write-chain (sdk-core build) → owned + shared write wiring → web-e2e enablement/triage.** Many `phase 65`-labelled stubs actually depend on the read-chain (subtree walks, key/childId/dest-key resolution): `downloadFromIpns`, version download, `collectChildKeys`, bin subtree collect, shared move/delete, owned `createFolder`. Assign waves accordingly.

**Shared-file serialization (critical):** MANY plans modify `packages/sdk/src/client.ts` and/or `packages/sdk-core/src/file/index.ts`. Two plans that edit the SAME file MUST NOT be in the same parallel wave (the executor runs a wave in parallel → conflict). Serialize client.ts-touching plans across waves, or group same-file work into one plan. `files_modified` frontmatter must be accurate — the wave scheduler depends on it.
</sequencing_and_waves>

<scope_fences>
- Runtime WIRING to existing primitives only; the only new sdk-core logic is the owned file write-chain (+ two tiny helpers permitted: publish-empty-root-Node, raw-`fileKey` download). NO new codec/crypto, NO change to the frozen `SealedChildRef`/`Node` read schema.
- **Delete** `packages/sdk/src/reencrypt.ts` (obsolete, no callers).
- ZERO new `apps/web/src/**/*.spec.ts` (SC#5). Web behavior proven ONLY by `tests/web-e2e` Playwright specs (most already exist — enabling them by making the runtime real is the point). Hoist testable logic to SDK (Vitest).
- OUT OF SCOPE: FUSE/WinFsp (Phase 69); Tier-3 capability layer.
- Zeroization (D-09): zero minted/derived keys on success + catch/finally; never zero caller-supplied buffers (see `shared-write.ts` `didDeriveWriteKey`).
- Cross-package build order: after sdk-core/sdk edits, rebuild dist before web typecheck/e2e.
</scope_fences>

<downstream_consumer>
Output consumed by /gsd-execute-phase. Every plan needs: frontmatter (`wave`, `depends_on`, `files_modified` accurate, `autonomous`, `requirements` ⊆ {WEB-01..04}); tasks in XML with `<read_first>` (incl. the file being modified + the shared-write.ts analog) and checkable `<acceptance_criteria>` (grep/source assertions, targeted vitest pass, `tsc -b` clean, or a named web-e2e spec passing); `<action>` with concrete identifiers (real fn names, file:line targets, `NodeContent`/`SealedChildRef` fields) and NO fenced full implementations; `<verify>`; `must_haves.truths` as observable LIVE-SYSTEM properties mapped goal-backward to WEB-01..04 and the 5 success criteria (e.g. "a new user logs in and reaches /files", "an uploaded file downloads with correct plaintext", "the full web-e2e suite passes"); and an **"Artifacts this phase produces"** section (new symbols: the sdk-core file write-chain fns, the root-Node-publish helper, raw-fileKey download, any FolderState field additions).

The final plan(s) must make SC#1 true: `grep -rn "not implemented — phase 6" packages/sdk/src apps/web/src` returns no live/reachable throws. Cover every capability group from RESEARCH (read a–d; write a–f). Include a final web-e2e enablement/triage plan whose gate is the full suite green.
</downstream_consumer>

**Granularity:** fine
**MVP_MODE:** false

Return `## PLANNING COMPLETE` with the plan count and a one-line-per-plan summary (id → objective → wave → requirements). If the scope genuinely exceeds a single phase's budget, return `## PHASE SPLIT RECOMMENDED` with a proposed read-phase/write-phase split.
